questions.q: What is the default Run if condition for a task with a depends_on entry?
options: All succeeded — every dependency must have succeeded
All done — regardless of dependency outcome
At least one failed
None failed
questions.explain: All succeeded is the default: a task only runs once every task it depends on has succeeded.

questions.q: Which Run if conditions make a real cleanup-or-alert task possible — one that runs because something broke?
options: At least one failed, and All failed
All succeeded, and None failed
All done only
There is no way to build this pattern with Run if conditions
questions.explain: These two conditions let a task run specifically because an upstream task failed, rather than despite it.

questions.q: What is fan-in, as described in this lesson?
options: Multiple upstream tasks that must all finish before one downstream task starts
One upstream task feeding multiple downstream tasks in parallel
A task that depends on itself
A cluster shared between multiple jobs
questions.explain: Fan-in is when a downstream task lists multiple dependencies, all of which must complete (by default, successfully) first.

questions.q: What status does a task get when its Run if condition is not met?
options: Excluded — skipped, not failed
Failed
Upstream failed
Succeeded
questions.explain: A task whose Run if condition isn't met is marked Excluded — a meaningfully different status from Failed.

questions.q: What happens to a task's own dependents when that task is marked Excluded?
options: By default, they are excluded too, cascading down the chain
They are automatically marked Failed
They always run regardless
The job stops entirely and cannot be resumed
questions.explain: Exclusion cascades: if a task is excluded, its dependents are typically excluded too, unless their own Run if condition says otherwise.
